Admitting Officer
Emergency Department
Children's Hospital
Newtown

18/01/2014

Dear Sir / Madam,
Re: Joshua Vance,                                       D.O.B:17/11/2013

Thank you for seeing Joshua, an 8½-week-old infant, who has mild dehydration along with a 5-day history      Comment [Benchmark1]: male
of absolute constipation. Your urgent management is highly appreciated.

Joshua is a male infant who was delivered through a normal vaginal delivery at the thirty-eight week of
gestation. Please note, he is his mother's first child.

On 31/12/2013, Joshua was brought by his mother for his routine six-week check. His weight was 3900
grams and he was in a good health except for mild constipation. Therefore, I advised her to express milk
from one feed then to be given to the baby in a bottle with some water. Two weeks later, There was no        Comment [Benchmark2]: give it
improvement regarding the constipation. Consequently, daily Coloxyl drops were commenced in addition         Comment [Benchmark3]: t
to one more feed to be added to him mixing with water. It is worth mentioning that in spite of not           Comment [Benchmark4]: of
completing his feeds, his weight increased to 4200 grams.                                                    Comment [Benchmark5]: ,diluted
                                                                                                             with some boiled cooled water, to be given
                                                                                                             to the baby.
Today, unfortunately, his mother reported that he had not passed any stool for five days. He had been
refusing feeds; and thus he lost 100 grams of his weight. His examination revealed mild generalized
abdominal tenderness, dry mucous membranes and skin turgor.

In light of the above, the patient is being referred for urgent rehydration and further assessment. Should
you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
